record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.original_question: Develop a theory of robust stable matchings for the Stable Roommates problem, including robustness notions analogous to those studied for Stable Marriage and incomplete-list variants, since robust stability in SR appears not to have been studied in those senses.

evidence.quote: As far as we are aware, robust stable matchings in sr have not been studied previously (either in the senses of Mai and Vazirani [66, 67] or Chen et al. [26]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Stable Roommates setting. Let $A=\{a_1,\dots,a_n\}$ be a finite set of agents with $n$ even. A preference profile $P$ assigns to each agent $a\in A$ a strict total order $\succ_a$ over $A\setminus\{a\}$ (the complete-list case), or a strict total order over some subset of $A\setminus\{a\}$ representing acceptable partners (the incomplete-list case). A matching is a partition $M$ of $A$ into pairs (and, in the incomplete-list case, possibly singletons). A pair $\{a,b\}\notin M$ is blocking if $a$ and $b$ each prefer the other to their partner in $M$ (with being unmatched ranked below every acceptable partner). $M$ is stable if it admits no blocking pair.

Two notions of robust stability have been studied for the Stable Marriage problem:

(i) Robustness to errors / swaps in preferences (Mai–Vazirani style). Given a preference profile $P$ and an integer $d\geq 0$, define the $d$-neighbourhood $N_d(P)$ to consist of all profiles $P'$ obtainable from $P$ by performing at most $d$ adjacent swaps in the preference lists (over all agents in total, or per agent, depending on the variant). A stable matching $M$ for $P$ is called $d$-robust if $M$ is stable in every $P'\in N_d(P)$, or, in a weaker variant, if for every $P'\in N_d(P)$ there exists a stable matching $M'$ for $P'$ that is "close" to $M$ in a prescribed sense (e.g. small symmetric difference).

(ii) Robustness to changes in preferences (Chen et al. style). Here one studies how stable matchings adapt to bounded modifications of the profile, parameterized by combinatorial measures of change, and asks for matchings simultaneously stable, or simultaneously "almost stable", across a set of profiles.

Task. Develop an analogous theory of robust stable matchings for the Stable Roommates problem, both with complete and with incomplete preference lists. In particular:

(a) Formulate precise definitions of $d$-robust stable matchings for Stable Roommates in the senses of (i) and (ii), accounting for the fact that some Stable Roommates instances admit no stable matching at all.

(b) Determine the computational complexity of deciding, given an instance $(A,P)$ of Stable Roommates and an integer $d$, whether a $d$-robust stable matching exists, and of finding one if it does.

(c) Establish structural results (existence guarantees, lattice or poset structure of robust stable matchings, characterizations of instances admitting robust stable matchings, bounds on the size of $d$ for which they exist) parallel to those known in the Stable Marriage case.

Provide such definitions, algorithms, hardness results, and structural theorems for Stable Roommates and its incomplete-list variants.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for robust stable matchings in the Stable Roommates problem returned no work developing the Mai–Vazirani or Chen et al. notions of robustness specifically for Stable Roommates. Existing robustness work (Mai–Vazirani ESA 2018; Chen et al.; Gangam's dissertation work) focuses on Stable Marriage / bipartite settings. A separate line of work introduces "stability against robust deviations" for the roommate problem, but this is a different notion (weakening stability via deviation depth), not the input-perturbation robustness asked for here. The problem therefore appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Finding Stable Matchings That Are Robust to Errors in the Input (Mai, Vazirani, ESA 2018)
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces robustness to errors in the input for stable matchings; the setting is bipartite (Stable Marriage).
status_evidence.claim: The robustness notion of Mai and Vazirani is developed for Stable Marriage, not Stable Roommates.

status_evidence.title: Stability against robust deviations in the roommate problem
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces SaRD, a weakening of stability for the roommate problem when no stable matching exists.
status_evidence.claim: Existing 'robustness' work for the roommate problem concerns deviation-depth robustness, a different concept than perturbation-of-input robustness.

status_evidence.title: Robust Stable Matchings: Dealing with Changes in Preferences (arXiv:2601.07959)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies robust stable matchings under changing preferences in the bipartite setting.
status_evidence.claim: Chen-style robustness for changing preferences has been developed for Stable Marriage but not for Stable Roommates.
